content.title: Demi Moore reflects on losing Best Actress at Oscars: 'Would have been wonderful' to win
content.text: Demi Moore received her first-ever Best Actress nomination for her role in The Substance.Anora's Mikey Madison eventually won the race at the Academy Awards."The physical, human part that has ego, of course, has disappointment," Moore said. From the Golden Globes to the SAG Awards, Demi Moore's recent awards season haul might've looked like a Monstro Elisasue-style heap of statuettes she collected along the way — but, after she ultimately lost the Oscar to Mikey Madison, the Hollywood icon has opened up about how she dealt with the development. In a new interview for TIME's annual list of the world's most influential people, the 62-year-old Substance star opened up about her feelings on the 2025 Academy Awards loss to Anora's Madison, which came in March after both women traveled the awards circuit in good favor with the industry. "The physical, human part that has ego, of course, has disappointment," Moore told the publication. "It certainly would have been wonderful to have won." The publication noted that the actress believes there's meaning in loss, though, that she'll use as she moves forward and walks through new doors in her subsequent career. "That's the beautiful thing when you really open up to how the universe really works, as opposed to gripping so tight, trying to force things to happen," she said near the end of the interview. "You really move with the flow." In an Instagram post shortly after the Oscars ceremony, Moore also congratulated Madison, who'd previously won the BAFTA Awards for Best Actress, on her victory. During the post, Moore wrote a "huge congratulations to #MikeyMadison" and told the star that she "can’t wait to see what you do next." Demi Moore in 'The Substance'. Christine Tamalet/Courtesy of TIFF Moore's trajectory through awards season began at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival in May, where her performance in The Substance earned a headline-making standing ovation from the prestigious event's crowd. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly shortly after the film's Cannes debut, Moore revealed that she once considered stepping away from acting altogether after feeling like she didn't have a place in the contemporary industry. She added: “I went through a period of even questioning whether this is what I should still be doing. In the last four years or so, I felt that it was a personal question that I wanted to explore and see. Was this where I should be putting my energy? When you plant seeds, you wait to see what grows.” Up next, following her sublime work in writer-director Coralie Fargeat's body-horror masterpiece The Substance, Moore will star in Boots Riley's new movie I Love Boosters, as well as season 2 of Tyler Sheridan's Landman TV series.
